To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the dielectric properties of nanostructured materials are strongly influenced by the local chemical environment and the presence of interfaces and that the local chemical environment also plays an important role in the electronic properties of these systems.

the local dielectric constant is a function of the chemical bonding environment, that band bending and band offsets can be correlated to the local chemical bonding environment, and that interfacial trap-states can be correlated to local chemical bonding environment and the local electronic structure.
the variation in local dielectric properties across interfaces is related to the chemical bonding environment at the interface.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a first-principles computational methodology that can accurately describe the dielectric and the electronic properties of technologically relevant nano-structured systems over length scales ranging from the inter-atomic distances to the macroscopic dimensions.
understanding and modeling of the local properties at the nanoscale in technologically important systems.
understanding the electronic and dielectric properties of nano-structured materials, with a focus on the effects of surfaces and interfaces.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the properties of nanodielectrics are determined by the local chemical environments of the constituent elements.
the properties of nanoscale dielectric systems are strongly affected by the surface and interfacial chemical environments, and the resulting local electronic structure.
the dielectric and electrical characteristics of nanoscale systems are highly sensitive to local atomic scale properties at interfaces and surfaces.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the dielectric properties of a nano-structured system can be predicted using the local dielectric constant, which can be computed from first principles using the theory of local dielectric permittance.
the local dielectric properties of nanodielectric systems are determined by the local atomic bonding environments.
the electronic and dielectric properties of nanoscale materials are strongly influenced by the atomic level chemical bonding environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the local dielectric constant and electronic structure of nanoscale materials can be very different from their bulk properties, and this difference has to be taken into account in order to accurately model their macroscopic properties.
first-principles computational methods are now sufficiently mature and efficient to be applied routinely in the analysis of local properties of nano-structured dielectrics.
the electronic and dielectric properties of nanostructured materials are highly sensitive to the local chemical environment at surfaces and interfaces.
